result:
Everything is healthy and I changed nothing this hour. The limit is that there isn't enough queued work, not any resource.

- **Running:** 4 FEBio runs (physrotFr2 p060, p062, p109 and p125), each pinned to its own 4 cores. All 4 logs were updated within 15 s of my check, and their simulation time is at 3.2–3.9.
- **Throughput:** 4 runs finished in the last 3 h, all with exit 0; the last one finished at 16:40.
- **Resources:**
  - CPU: we use 8.4 of our 32 cores, with no new throttling.
  - Memory: 58 of 128 GB, and no out-of-memory kills.
  - GPUs: none of the 7 are ours. GPUs 1–4 are 98–99 % busy with other users' work, and GPUs 0, 5 and 6 are idle but mostly hold other users' memory.
  - Disk: 1.5 TB free (89 % full).
- **Queues:** nothing is waiting in either queue. The FEBio queue has 2268 done and 2 failed. The new task queue has 1 done and 5 failed, all from 10-28, and nothing has run there since.
- **Services:** all 6 tmux services that `ops/resume_all.sh` should keep up are running. The 3 one-off jobs it can also start (biocage_physio_v3, biocage_physio_rot, rot_chain) are correctly absent because they are marked finished.
- **Restart cover:** the 4 running jobs are tracked by the FEBio queue and resume from their checkpoints.
- **Idle:** about 23 cores and 70 GB are free now, and all 32 cores will be free when the 4 physrotFr2 runs finish.
- **Needs a person:**
  - Queue more computations.
  - Decide the items still open from earlier reports: T01, T16, T10 (a disk guard for the FEBio scheduler) and the al_loop gate.
